rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read all 11 expanded chunks in order. Closest candidates resolve: chunk 4 line 24 'between them' follows the six agents named in the same paragraph; chunk 10 line 100 'it' is the thing just built and 'that' is the access to the systems named in the immediately preceding sentence. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Named document links appear in chunk 2 line 8 and chunk 9 lines 93-95. 'Last module' at chunk 4 line 24 is module-arc framing, not a callback to another file by opening/page position; no unnamed positional callback appears.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No specific 'the X you did/saw/caught' backward-beat construction appears in the body; the two prompt blocks are fenced and exempt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-before-reveal instruction appears in the body; the prompt code blocks are fenced and exempt.

Every rendered chunk carries a claim, list, instruction, logistics handoff, or forward action. The shortest substantive chunks, chunk 1 'Big Idea' and chunk 10 'Next', each carry self-standing claims; the title chunk is the deck's title slide, not a wait-state.

All headers match the content in their own chunks: 'Optional memory check before Module 4' names the optional health-check action at chunk 7, and 'Next' names the forward handoff at chunk 10. No header is contradicted by its chunk.

Manual body-only sweep, excluding fenced prompts: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction, empty anaphora/epistrophe triple, self-grading superlative, number-plus-retraction, abstraction-noun stack, or empty-leg verb triplet. Chunk 4's 'searched... pulled... chased down' is concrete retrieval work, not a cadence tic.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Full body read found no repo-internal 'compendium', 'firing', 'forcing function', 'beat', 'mood', or surface-as-noun usage. 'Dialect' at chunk 3 line 13 and chunk 8 line 86 describes each source's language as a teaching concept; session/task, rules file, retrieval files, and training directory are student-facing artifacts, not maintainer jargon.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 8 'Key Concepts', lines 85-89, opens every bullet with a bolded full-sentence claim: '**Two multi-agent shapes.**', '**Splitting earns its keep when the agents genuinely can't be one.**', '**Seams are where it fails.**', '**Three stances beat one summarizer.**', and '**Frameworks are the synthesizer's spine.**' The compendium's LO exception covers What You'll Learn, not this consolidation slide; this is the rule's explicitly banned every-bullet-bolded-lead shape.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Leave the concept claims in plain text or bold only short concept handles; preserve the explanatory prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The module's headings are architecture labels plus allowed orientation/logistics/action forms: Start here (orientation), Push back on the summary (imperative), Optional memory check before Module 4 (named optional action), and Next (closer).
